title: Evolve AL Interfaces with Default Implementations in Business Central 29.0
summary: Business Central 29.0 introduces default method implementations for AL interfaces, allowing interface contracts to evolve without immediately breaking existing implementations. The feature works with RequiredPending and analyzer rules to create a staged migration path where interface authors can add new methods with fallback behavior and gradually require explicit implementations over time.
key_points: Interfaces can now provide default method bodies, preventing immediate breaking changes when new methods are added
RequiredPending and analyzer rules enable a staged migration where implementations gradually shift from using defaults to providing explicit implementations
This feature reduces impact on extension ecosystems where many independent implementations depend on shared interfaces
Default implementations should only be used when a sensible fallback behavior exists, not to avoid implementation requirements
Interface evolution can now separate concerns between backward compatibility and controlled contract strengthening

quotes.text: With a default implementation, the interface method can contain a method body that provides fallback behavior.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core mechanism that enables backward compatibility when interfaces evolve
